Plot the simulated Q3 residual correlations

Source: R/locdep_q3_plot.R
RMlocdepQ3plot.Rd

Plots the simulated \(Q_3\) of each item pair from RMlocdepQ3Cutoff(), and optionally the observed \(Q_3\) in your data and a heatmap of the observed matrix.

Usage

RMlocdepQ3Plot(simfit, data, items = NULL, n_pairs = NULL)

Arguments

simfit

The result of RMlocdepQ3Cutoff().

data

Optional. The item responses the simulations were made from, items scored from 0. The observed \(Q_3\) is then computed with the estimator of simfit and drawn as orange diamonds, and the heatmap is returned.

items

Optional character vector of item names. Only pairs with both items in it are shown. Default NULL, all pairs.

n_pairs

Optional positive integer. Only the n_pairs pairs with the largest departure are shown: |observed - simulated median| with data, |simulated median| without. Applied after items. Values above the number of pairs show all pairs.

Value

A named list of two ggplot objects, with the same structure as the tables of RMlocdepQ3():

pairs

one row per item pair, labelled "Item1 - Item2".

matrix

a heatmap of the lower triangle of the observed \(Q_3\) matrix, with pairs above the global dynamic cutoff outlined. It needs data, so it is NULL (with a message) without it. With items, it shows those items only. n_pairs does not apply to it.

Details

\(Q_3\) is symmetric, so each pair is shown once (unlike partial gamma, which depends on the direction).

Each pair's simulated values are drawn as dots, with the median, an inner 66% interval and an outer interval. The outer interval is the one in simfit$pair_cutoffs, which RMlocdepQ3() tabulates: the HDCI of width hdci_width, or the 2.5th to 97.5th percentiles with cutoff_method = "quantile". The inner interval uses the same method. Without data the intervals are drawn with ggdist::stat_dotsinterval(). With data they are black segments with a black dot for the median, and the observed value is an orange diamond.

The intervals are per pair and not corrected for testing many pairs. With the full cutoff object, RMlocdepQ3() flags pairs by adjusted p-values instead, so a pair just outside its interval need not be flagged there. The plot shows no p-values.

The ggplot2, ggdist and scales packages must be installed, and mirt for estimator = "MML".

See also

RMlocdepQ3(), RMlocdepQ3Cutoff(), RMlocdepGammaPlot()

Examples

# \donttest{
if (requireNamespace("ggplot2", quietly = TRUE) &&
    requireNamespace("ggdist", quietly = TRUE)) {
  set.seed(42)
  sim_data <- as.data.frame(
    matrix(sample(0:1, 200 * 10, replace = TRUE), nrow = 200, ncol = 10)
  )
  colnames(sim_data) <- paste0("Item", 1:10)

  # Run the simulation (use 1000 or more iterations in real analyses)
  cutoff_res <- RMlocdepQ3Cutoff(sim_data, iterations = 50,
                                 parallel = FALSE, seed = 42)

  # Simulated distribution only
  RMlocdepQ3Plot(cutoff_res)

  # With observed Q3 overlaid
  RMlocdepQ3Plot(cutoff_res, data = sim_data)

  # Top 10 pairs by departure from null
  RMlocdepQ3Plot(cutoff_res, data = sim_data, n_pairs = 10)
}
#> The Q3 tile heatmap ($matrix) requires `data`; returning $matrix = NULL.
